tools.name: Visual Studio Code
tools.description: A free, open-source-based code editor from Microsoft with extensions for almost every language.
tools.note: Install the Python or Live Server extension to get started fast.

tools.name: Git
tools.description: The version control system that tracks every change to your code.
tools.note: Learn four commands first: init, add, commit, log.

tools.name: GitHub
tools.description: Hosts Git repositories, with issues, pull requests and free public projects.
tools.note: Students can apply for the GitHub Student Developer Pack.

tools.name: Python
tools.description: A beginner-friendly programming language used for scripting, data, AI and the web.
tools.note: Start in IDLE or VS Code, then try small scripts.

tools.name: Node.js
tools.description: Runs JavaScript outside the browser, for servers and tools.
tools.note: Install the LTS version.

tools.name: Replit
tools.description: Code in the browser in many languages, with nothing to install.
tools.note: Good for school computers where you cannot install software.

tools.name: Jupyter
tools.description: Notebooks that mix code, results and notes. Popular for data and AI.
tools.note: Try JupyterLab or use notebooks inside VS Code.

tools.name: Google Colab
tools.description: Free Jupyter notebooks in the cloud, with optional GPU time.
tools.note: Free GPU time is limited; save your work to Drive.

tools.name: Kaggle
tools.description: Datasets, notebooks, competitions and short courses for data science.
tools.note: Start with the Learn section.

tools.name: freeCodeCamp
tools.description: A free curriculum for web development, Python and data, with projects.
tools.note: Build every project yourself, not just the lessons.

tools.name: Khan Academy
tools.description: Free lessons in maths, computing and science.
tools.note: Great for revising maths for programming.

tools.name: Figma
tools.description: Design interfaces and prototypes in the browser, together.
tools.note: Education plans exist for students and teachers.

tools.name: Canva
tools.description: Quick graphics, posters and presentations from templates.
tools.note: Canva for Education is free for eligible schools.

tools.name: Inkscape
tools.description: Open-source vector graphics editor.
tools.note: Export SVG for websites.

tools.name: GIMP
tools.description: Open-source image editor.
tools.note: Use layers so you can undo changes.

tools.name: Blender
tools.description: Open-source 3D modelling, animation and rendering.
tools.note: Follow a beginner tutorial series start to finish.

tools.name: Notion
tools.description: Notes, to-do lists and wikis in one place.
tools.note: Make one page per subject.

tools.name: Obsidian
tools.description: Markdown notes stored as files on your own device.
tools.note: Free for personal use; sync is paid.

tools.name: Trello
tools.description: Boards and cards to plan projects.
tools.note: Use columns: To do, Doing, Done.

tools.name: Google Workspace for Education
tools.description: Docs, Sheets, Slides and Classroom for schools.
tools.note: Ask your school whether you already have access.

tools.name: PostgreSQL
tools.description: A powerful open-source relational database.
tools.note: Learn SQL basics: SELECT, WHERE, JOIN.

tools.name: SQLite
tools.description: A small database stored in a single file.
tools.note: Python includes it: import sqlite3.

tools.name: DB Browser for SQLite
tools.description: A visual tool to open and edit SQLite databases.
tools.note: Good for seeing your tables while learning SQL.

tools.name: MySQL Community Edition
tools.description: The free edition of the popular MySQL database.
tools.note: Often used with PHP.

tools.name: GitHub Pages
tools.description: Free hosting for static websites from a GitHub repository.
tools.note: Perfect for a first website.

tools.name: Netlify
tools.description: Deploys websites from Git with a free starter plan.
tools.note: Drag and drop a folder to publish.

tools.name: Vercel
tools.description: Hosts websites and serverless functions with a free hobby plan.
tools.note: Connect a GitHub repo for automatic deploys.

tools.name: Microsoft Azure for Students
tools.description: Free cloud credit and services for eligible students.
tools.note: Check eligibility on the site; no credit card needed for students.

tools.name: Docker
tools.description: Packages apps with everything they need to run.
tools.use: Running apps the same way everywhere
tools.note: Docker Desktop is free for personal and education use.

tools.name: Postman
tools.description: Send and test API requests without writing code.
tools.note: Try a public API first, like a weather API.

tools.name: Selenium
tools.description: Open-source browser automation for testing websites.
tools.note: Start with the Python bindings.

tools.name: Playwright
tools.description: Open-source end-to-end testing for modern web apps.
tools.note: Its code generator records your clicks as a test.

tools.name: Wireshark
tools.description: Captures and inspects network traffic packet by packet.
tools.note: Only capture traffic on networks you are allowed to.

tools.name: Cisco Packet Tracer
tools.description: Network simulator for building and testing virtual networks.
tools.note: Needs a free Cisco Networking Academy account.

tools.name: Nmap
tools.description: Open-source network scanner.
tools.note: Only scan networks you own or have permission to test.

tools.name: VirtualBox
tools.description: Runs other operating systems in a window on your computer.
tools.note: Give the virtual machine at least 2 GB of RAM.

tools.name: Ubuntu
tools.description: A popular, beginner-friendly Linux distribution.
tools.note: Try it in VirtualBox before installing.

tools.name: Claude
tools.description: An AI assistant for explanations, writing help and code review.
tools.note: Use AI to understand, then do the work yourself.

tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.description: An AI assistant for questions, explanations and drafts.
tools.note: Check facts: AI can be wrong.

tools.name: Hugging Face
tools.description: Open AI models, datasets and demos.
tools.note: Try models in the browser through Spaces.

tools.name: Scratch
tools.description: Block-based coding from MIT for first-time programmers.
tools.note: Great for learning loops and events.

tools.name: Discord
tools.description: Chat servers for communities and study groups.
tools.note: Check age rules and privacy settings.
